response: Yes, there is still a need for living-related liver transplantation (LRT) in children, particularly in urgent cases where a cadaveric graft cannot be found in time or when the optimal time point for transplantation is crucial. Although the short- and long-term outcomes after LRT and deceased donor liver transplantation (SLT) do not differ significantly, SLT is considered the first-line therapy in countries where cadaveric organs are available due to the risk to the living donor in LRT. However, LRT provides a vital solution in situations where a cadaveric graft is not available, making it still a necessary option in pediatric liver transplantation.
